metadata.body:
## Problem TypeScript and TSX functions often end too early, too late, or disappear. On stash (a React/TSX code base), lizard reports only about half of the functions with their correct start and end lines. Several parser faults are involved, and they partly cancel each other out, so fixing one alone moves the error elsewhere. This pull request fixes them together. ## Causes and fixes 1. **Return types.** `CodeStateMachine.__call__` cleared `self.callback` after running it, which dropped the callback the old one had just set. After a simple return type (`): void {`), the body's end handler was lost and the function ended at the next statement. The callback is now taken before it runs. Only TypeScript has a callback that feeds a token back into the machine (`_consume_type_annotation`), so no other reader changes; the suite and corpora in Python, C, Java, Go, and JavaScript are unchanged. 2. **Optional calls.** After `.`, `_field` took the next token as a field name, so `f?.(x)` and `a?.[i]` swallowed the opening bracket. 3. **JSX tags.** The tag reader aborted on hyphenated names (`data-action`), attributes without a value (``, ``), spread attributes (`{...props}`), member names with attributes (``), and type arguments (` value={v}>`). An abort replayed an attribute's `{` without its `}`, and the replayed tokens bypassed the enclosing brace count, so components ran to the end of the file or lost a `}` (``). 4. **Order and lines in JSX.** Attribute expressions reached the state machine before the tag's own text, and newlines inside a tag were held back until it ended. Functions inside multi-line tags got lines up to 13 too early, and `c = ( g(v)} />)` read as an arrow `c = (v) => …`. The tag text read so far now goes out before each attribute expression, and newlines go out immediately. 5. **Expression-bodied arrows.** They started on the line after `=>` when the body began there, and in an object or argument list they ended on the next line instead of at their `,`. 6. **Parenthesized expressions.** `x = (function () {…})()` and `c = (
…
)` were read as the parameter list of an arrow named `x` or `c`. 7. **Comparisons in JSX.** `{i < n}` after a tag is read as an object literal, where `<` started type parameters that never closed. ## Verification Function spans from the TypeScript compiler (`ts.createSourceFile`, every function-like node with a body) serve as the reference. A function counts as found when lizard reports it in the same file with the same end line and a start on its declaration or its own line. `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.js`, `.jsx`, and `.mjs` files are included. "Unmatched" counts lizard entries that match no compiler span. | Code base | Exact, master | Exact, this PR | Unmatched, master | Unmatched, this PR | |---|---|---|---|---| | stash | 51.0 % | 90.5 % | 2757 | 662 | | anki | 69.4 % | 88.9 % | 506 | 138 | | a private TypeScript host | 73.8 % | 87.0 % | 180 | 60 | | jupyterlab-desktop | 86.9 % | 90.5 % | 195 | 121 | | KaTeX | 94.2 % | 95.8 % | 77 | 48 | This PR finds 3900 functions exactly that master misses; master finds 3 that this PR misses. In two of the three I traced, master is right only because a second fault offsets the first; for example, in `reviews.ts` an IIFE as an object value ends the enclosing function early on both sides, and master's other faults happen to undo it. I can share the two small scripts behind these numbers. - 18 new tests in `testTypeScript.py` and `testTSX.py`. All but one fail on master; the exception guards object types inside type arguments (`Promise<{ a: T; b: U }>`), which master handles. - Two existing tokenizer tests, `test_with_embeded_attributes` and `test_complicated_properties`, now expect the tag text before the attribute expression. That old order was one of the causes above. - Full suite passes; `pycodestyle` is clean; pylint on the three changed files goes from 9.39 to 9.45. ## Relation to #518 #518 (optional chaining in CCN) and this PR touch different parts of `typescript.py` and merge cleanly. Merged together, the suite passes and the numbers above stay the same. Both append test classes at the end of `testTypeScript.py` and `testTSX.py`, so the second to land conflicts there; keeping both sides resolves it. ## Not covered - Multi-line expression bodies still end at their first line break. - An IIFE as an object value (`p: (() => {…})()`) still ends the enclosing function early.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Stop at replayed JSX-expression closing braces**

When an XML candidate inside an attribute expression aborts on its closing `}`, this branch adjusts `depth` to zero but neither stops the `TSXTokenizer` nor suppresses that terminator as `JSTokenizer.process_token` does. For `const e = <D visible={p.i < p.n} />` inside a component, `analyze_source_code` therefore replays `}` into the TypeScript state and reports the component ending on that attribute line, so following branches are omitted from its span and CCN. Stop when the adjusted depth reaches zero so the attribute wrapper can finish normally.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep body-internal commas inside the arrow**

This closes every expression-bodied arrow at every comma, including commas that belong to the expression rather than to the surrounding property or argument list. For `const f = () => [1, x ? 2 : 3]`, high-level analysis now assigns only the prefix to `f` and drops the ternary from its CCN; a multiline `function f(): () => [number, number] { ... }` is even ended on its declaration line because the return type's `=>` sets this flag. Track delimiter/type context and pop only for an actual enclosing-list separator.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Parse optional indexes outside member-name collection**

In a class or object field initializer, redispatching `[` to `_state_global` enters the existing `as_object` computed-member-name path, whose collector consumes everything through `]` without parsing it. As a result, `analyze_source_code` drops the callback in `class C { value = callbacks?.[items.findIndex(item => item.ok)]; method() {} }`, whereas it was reported before this branch; optional index contents need an expression substate rather than the member-name collector.
